founder.name: Marcus Abel
founder.background_summary: 7-year UCSF ICU nurse, 3 years as charge nurse. Left clinical work ~1 year ago to teach himself to code and build tooling for ICU shift-change handoffs, anchored by a 2022 patient-safety event he witnessed.
founder.current_status: Per-diem nursing shifts to cover bills while self-studying (Codecademy ~6 months) and designing a handoff tool.

archetype_mix.rationale: Deep, narrow, years-long obsession with a specific clinical workflow failure (Hound). Charge-nurse operator experience managing cross-functional surge events shows Hustler muscle but untested outside clinical walls. Tutorial-level self-taught coding — Hacker weighting is minimal and should not be relied on for shipping.

evidence: SBAR handoffs that are supposed to be 5 min routinely run 20 min; can articulate the why (EHR doesn't surface last vasopressor change, ventilator settings evolution, family communication status).
Nurse 'brain sheet' paper workflow that exists outside the system of record and is discarded at end of shift.
Epic Rover is the incumbent mobile surface and is functional but insufficient.
Structural contrast between trauma ICU rounding (single-provider) vs cardiac ICU (multidisciplinary: CT surgery + cardiology + ICU fellow) and the political friction around extubation decisions.
Cites Joint Commission sentinel-event data: communication failures underlie ~60-70% of adverse events.
market_edge.notes: This is arcana only available via lived insider experience. Strongest dimension of the profile.

evidence: 6 months of Codecademy.
Built one tutorial-following React + Flask to-do app.
Self-reports he could not ship an MVP solo in 72 hours.
No prior shipped production systems, no public code portfolio, no systems design signals.
calibration_notes: Honestly self-reported — credibility intact, capability not.
Cannot be the founding engineer. Should not try to close the gap by studying longer.
Healthcare adds integration complexity (FHIR, HL7, SMART on FHIR, Epic/Cerner APIs, HIPAA BAA, SOC2) that requires senior engineering judgment from day one.

evidence: Charge nurse for 3 years at UCSF ICU — coordinated 30+ patient handoffs during COVID surge.
Mediated physician-nurse conflicts under live clinical pressure.
Owned cross-functional relationships with bed control and pharmacy.
Ran the floor during crisis events.
gaps: No vendor or partnership negotiation outside the hospital.
No public speaking, no conference presence, no podcast or written media.
No demonstrated ability to rally capital or external talent.
catalyst_edge.notes: Internal clinical catalyst ability is probable and real. Founder-grade external catalyst ability is untested.

evidence: 7 years in a single top-tier ICU (UCSF).
3 years in a leadership role (charge nurse).
Personally witnessed a patient death from a handoff failure in 2022 — the founding story is real, dated, and specific.
Has independently synthesized a problem thesis (EHR fails to capture narrative handoff context) that matches the academic literature he's been reading.
Can name the incumbent tool (Epic Rover) and articulate where it stops being useful.
Distinguishes trauma vs cardiac ICU workflow structurally, not just anecdotally.

pillar_scores.composite_note: Profile is heavily spiked on domain + obsession, deeply underweight on network and shipping capability. Classic domain-first solo founder shape that needs a technical co-founder and a GTM bridge.

communities.name: Ex-ICU nurses (3 private Slack groups)
communities.notes: Member but not active. Potential seed of early users or ex-clinician healthtech operator intros, but not a buyer pipeline.

floor_nurses.notes: Strong — but not buyers of hospital software.

network.flag: Knows users, does not know buyers. Hospital enterprise software is one of the longest and most committee-driven B2B sales motions in the market, and Marcus has zero warm surface on that committee.

motivations.note_not_averaged: High missionary, very low mercenary — these are reported independently and should not be collapsed into a single value.
evidence: Explicit founding story: patient died from a handoff miss in 2022; cannot stop thinking about it.
States he would build this unpaid.
States he does not care about exit size.
Cares about the specific problem, not category or outcome.
risks_from_profile: May resist pivots away from the exact problem shape.
May undervalue commercial fit and underprice the product.
May have friction with VC-style growth pressure.

signals: 9+ months reading ICU handoff-error literature; can cite Joint Commission sentinel event findings from memory.
Left a stable UCSF career to pursue this.
Reads problem literature without being asked or assigned.

evidence: Charge-nurse temperament is crisis coordination, not steady-state optimization.
Obsession is pre-product and pre-validation.
Technical and commercial gaps make any scaling-stage context a poor fit.
No stated appetite for building or managing a large team.

constraints.runway_flag: TIGHT — shorter than a single hospital procurement cycle (typically 9-18 months). First 8-10 weeks of runway are decisive for co-founder, design partner, and fundraising.
constraints.employment: Per-diem nursing to cover living expenses

credibility_flags.flag: Self-claim to 'build an MVP with a co-founder' is plausible as a product-minded collaborator but not as a shipping engineer. Tutorial-level React/Flask will not survive healthcare integration and compliance work.
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: Find a senior full-stack co-founder with regulated-industry or healthcare background. Do not close this gap by continuing to self-study.

credibility_flags.flag: Knows users (floor nurses), does not know buyers (CMIO, CNIO, CIO, nursing VPs, procurement, health system innovation leads, healthcare investors).
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: Publish publicly on ICU handoff failure to generate inbound; use ex-ICU-nurse Slack to source ex-clinician healthtech operator intros; attend AMIA / HIMSS nursing informatics events to build CNIO surface.

credibility_flags.flag: No talks, no publications, no public writing. No external proof of expertise beyond the interview itself.
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: 6 months of consistent public writing plus one design-partner pilot would close most of this.

credibility_flags.flag: Charge-nurse operator ability is real internally. Founder-grade external catalyst (fundraising, hiring, partnerships, BD) is unobserved.
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: First external test: land one formal design-partner ICU unit and one pre-seed check. Both are forcing functions for external catalyst skill.

credibility_flags.flag: Building from grief is a real engine, but watch for rigidity about solution shape (e.g. standalone app vs Epic-embedded module). Ensure ability to hear disconfirming buyer feedback.
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: Design-partner feedback loop every 2 weeks; explicit written hypothesis log so the solution shape is allowed to change while the problem stays fixed.

credibility_flags.flag: 6-month personal runway is shorter than a hospital procurement cycle. Cannot self-fund to a paid contract.
credibility_flags.recommended_mitigation: Pre-seed raise ($500k-$1.5M) on the strength of domain + co-founder + design-partner LOI within the first ~60 days.

calibration_notes: Founder was honest about technical limits; self-awareness is high and should be rewarded in evaluation, not penalized as weakness.
Market-edge arcana is dense enough that a subject-matter-expert interviewer would likely confirm insider status within minutes.
Missionary and mercenary are reported independently, not averaged.
Profile is highly coachable on network and insider-markers; profile is not coachable on technical edge within a useful timeframe — this must be co-founded.
shape_one_liner: Domain-first mission-driven solo founder with elite insider market edge and elite obsession, but low shipping capability and no buyer network — needs a senior technical co-founder and a GTM bridge into hospital buying committees before the 6-month runway burns.
